title: WPMS/813/2016 of State Of Uttarakhand Vs Ganesh Pant

paras.text:
WPMS No. 813 of 2016
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. I.P. Kohli, Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand/petitioner.
This writ petition already stands abated by
the judgement of the coordinate Bench of this
Court, as rendered on 14.07.2020.
The petitioner herein has filed a Substitution
Application No. 6126/2020 with Delay
Condonation Application No. 6127/2020, as well
as an application to set aside the abatement No.
6128/2020, along with Recall Application No.
327/2020, seeking recall of the order dated
14.07.2020, and to set aside the abatement of the
writ petition.
When the substitution application was filed,
it had revealed that apart from the fact that it has
been filed with delay of 1830 days; but the
apparent fact which has reflected is that the heirs
of deceased respondent No. 1, who is being sought
to be brought on record by the substitution
application now in an abated writ petition; could
not be considered for the reason being even when
the writ petition was preferred by the petitioner on
30.03.2016, it was preferred almost after more than
one year after the death of respondent No. 1, who
is reported to have died on 12.03.2015.
In fact, there could not have been any writ
petition filed under the eyes of law against a dead
person and since this writ petition, right from its
inception is a nonest proceedings, having been
instituted against a deceased person, it has been
rightly abated by the coordinate Bench of this
Court by the order dated 14.07.2020, it does not
call for any reason to recall the said order, the
recall application is accordingly rejected.

Consequently, the substitution application,
delay condonation application and setting aside
abatement application are also rejected, because
the same cannot be filed in a proceedings which is
not in existence in the eyes of law.
Having dismissed the writ petition as having
abated, since being preferred against dead person,
will not preclude the petitioner to have his
appropriate recourses available, in accordance with
law, including filing of afresh writ petition, if
permissible after bringing the appropriate heirs on
record.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 18.08.2020 Mahinder/
